translationRepairs: Book of Sui, 56th year of Volume, 21th year of Biography
s0001 隋書卷五十六列傳第二十一 names Volume 56 and Biography 21; 卷 and 列傳 are not years.
Before this, envoys had often followed Chen court etiquette. When Kai led the mission, he adhered entirely to Sui protocol, and the Chen side could not make him yield.
Before this, envoys had often followed Chen court etiquette. When Kai led the mission, he adhered entirely to his own court's protocol, and the Chen side could not make him yield.
s0021 一依本朝 follows a Zhou embassy to Chen, still before Kaihuang, so 本朝 is Kai's own court, not Sui.

At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was given the additional title Pillar of State, Third Rank, dismissed as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced in rank to Marquis, and still acted as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was given the additional title Pillar of State, Third Rank, appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced in rank to Marquis, and still acted as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
s0025 除尚書吏部侍郎 is an appointment formula; 除 means to appoint, not to dismiss.
The prosecutors reported: "Fang Gongyi was a partisan of Yuwen Jiong and should never have been promoted.
The prosecutors reported: "Fang Gongyi was a partisan of Yuchi Jiong and should never have been promoted.
s0035 尉遲迥 is Yuchi Jiong; the original Yuwen Jiong invents the wrong surname.

Since Zhou times official selection had made no distinction between worthy and unworthy. When Kai took charge of personnel, he worked with Xue Daoheng and Lu Yanshi to sort the gentry by merit, and thus provoked the slander of She Danggu—which brought him to this end.

Since Zhou times official selection had made no distinction between worthy and unworthy. When Kai took charge of personnel, he worked with Xue Daoheng and Lu Yanshi to sort the gentry by merit, and thus incurred the slander of forming a solid clique—which brought him to this end.
s0048 故涉黨固之譖 is implication in slander of factional solidarity, not a person named She Danggu.

From the Zhou dynasty onward selection had no distinction of pure and impure; when Kai acted in the Ministry of Personnel, he with Xue Daoheng, Lu Yanshi, and others discriminated among the gentry streams, and so he fell under the slanders of the faction of She Danggu.

From the Zhou dynasty onward selection had no distinction of pure and impure; when Kai acted in the Ministry of Personnel, he with Xue Daoheng, Lu Yanshi, and others discriminated among the gentry streams, and so he fell under slanders of clique-forming.
s0048 黨固之譖 is slander about clique-forming, not the faction of a named She Danggu.

At the battle of Heyin an edict ordered him to serve while still in mourning garb. On his return he was appointed senior clerk in the bureau of appointments, inherited the title Duke of Pengyang, and received a fief of twenty-one hundred households.

At the battle of Heyin an edict ordered him to serve while still in mourning garb. On his return he was appointed junior grand master of the Bureau of Operations, inherited the title Duke of Pengyang, and received a fief of twenty-one hundred households.
s0062 職方下大夫 is junior grand master of Zhifang (operations), not a senior clerk of appointments.

In the campaign at Heyin, an edict ordered him to serve in ink-stained mourning garb; on return he was appointed Senior Clerk in the Bureau of Appointments, inherited the rank of Duke of Pengyang County, with a fief of 2,100 households.

In the campaign at Heyin, an edict ordered him to serve in ink-stained mourning garb; on return he was appointed Junior Grand Master of the Bureau of Operations, inherited the rank of Duke of Pengyang County, with a fief of 2,100 households.
s0062 職方下大夫 is the Bureau of Operations junior grand master; appointments is a mistranslation of 職方.
When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, Xi served in his existing post as acting chief censor.
When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, Xi served in his existing post as acting Neiyan.
s0065 以本官行納言事 is acting nayan, the inner-court spokesman, not chief censor.
At the moment Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Xi acted in the duties of Chief Censor in his original post.
At the moment Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Xi acted in the duties of Neiyan in his original post.
s0065 納言 is nayan, not the censorate office of Chief Censor.
He ordered Dou Lutong, governor of Xiangzhou, to adopt Xi's methods.
He ordered Doulu Tong, governor of Xiangzhou, to adopt Xi's methods.
s0084 豆盧通 uses the compound surname 豆盧; Dou Lutong splits it wrongly.
He ordered Governor of Xiangzhou Dou Lutong to study Xi's methods.
He ordered Governor of Xiangzhou Doulu Tong to study Xi's methods.
s0084 豆盧 is the Xianbei compound surname Doulu, so the name is Doulu Tong.
He rose repeatedly to pillar of state, was soon appointed senior clerk in the bureau of metals, and later received the additional rank of pillar of state.
He rose repeatedly to Shang Yitong, was soon appointed daifu of the Bureau of Metals, and later received the additional rank of kaifu.
s0120 累遷上儀同…後加開府 names Shang Yitong and kaifu, two ranks distinct from 柱國; 司金大夫 is not a clerk.
He was summoned as grand master for imperial entertainments, soon transferred to grand master for law. He applied the law with breadth and fairness and was regarded as competent in office.
He was summoned as Chamberlain of the Palace Guards, soon transferred to Chamberlain for Law Enforcement. He applied the law with breadth and fairness and was regarded as competent in office.
s0141 衛尉卿 is Chamberlain of the Palace Guards and 大理卿 Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, not imperial-entertainment titles.

Governor Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou. Zhou feared Liang's military edge and did not dare refuse. Liang then led troops to attack Zhou. Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to tell Liang, "Affairs under Heaven are not yet settled. Zhou, as a minister, must choose his stand according to what is fitting. Why rush to attack one another?"

Governor Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou. Zhou feared Prince Liang's military edge and did not dare refuse. Qi Liang then led troops to attack Zhou. Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to tell Qi Liang, "Affairs under Heaven are not yet settled. Zhou, as a minister, must choose his stand according to what is fitting. Why rush to attack one another?"
s0148 contrasts 諒 (Prince Liang) with 良 (Qi Liang), which the original collapses; after 請援, 不敢拒 is not daring to refuse aid, not a free rewrite as resist.
He had sons named He and Xian, both of whom became well known.
He had sons named Zi and Xian, both of whom became well known.
s0153 有子、獻 names sons 子 and 獻; 子 is Zi, not He.

Later he followed the emperor in pacifying Qi. For his merit he was appointed pillar of state, enfeoffed as duke of Wuwei county with a fief of fifteen hundred households, granted fifteen hundred bolts of goods, a hundred fifty slaves and maidservants, and more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and was made registrar to the governor-general of Si prefecture.

Later he followed the emperor in pacifying Qi. For his merit he was appointed Senior Yitong, enfeoffed as duke of Wuwei county with a fief of fifteen hundred households, granted fifteen hundred bolts of goods, a hundred fifty slaves and maidservants, and more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and was made registrar to the governor-general of Si prefecture.
s0172 拜上儀同 is Senior Yitong, not the separate honor 柱國 (pillar of state).

Later he followed the Emperor in pacifying Qi; for merit he was appointed Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei County with a fief of 1,500 households, granted 1,500 bolts of goods, 150 slaves and maidservants, and over a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and appointed Registrar to the Governor-General of Si Prefecture.

Later he followed the Emperor in pacifying Qi; for merit he was appointed Senior Yitong, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei County with a fief of 1,500 households, granted 1,500 bolts of goods, 150 slaves and maidservants, and over a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and appointed Registrar to the Governor-General of Si Prefecture.
s0172 上儀同 is Senior Yitong; rendering it Pillar of State conflates two Zhou-Sui ranks.
He was appointed governor of Huai prefecture and soon transferred to governor of South Si prefecture.
He was appointed governor of Kuai prefecture and soon transferred to governor of South Si prefecture.
s0182 澮州刺史 is Kuai prefecture (澮), not Huai (淮).
He was appointed Governor of Huai Prefecture and soon transferred to Governor of South Si Prefecture.
He was appointed Governor of Kuai Prefecture and soon transferred to Governor of South Si Prefecture.
s0182 澮州 is Kuai, distinct from 淮州; the literal Huai is the wrong graph.
He received the additional rank pillar of state, was promoted to minister of punishments, and led the crown prince's guard of honored attendants.
He received the additional rank of Kaifu, was promoted to minister of punishments, and led the crown prince's guard of honored attendants.
s0192 加開府 adds the Kaifu honor, not 柱國 pillar of state.
He was given the additional rank Pillar of State, promoted and appointed Minister of Punishments, and led the Crown Prince's Guard of Honored Attendants.
He was given the additional rank of Kaifu, promoted and appointed Minister of Punishments, and led the Crown Prince's Guard of Honored Attendants.
s0192 開府 is Kaifu; Pillar of State is a different rank.

At that time the emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns. Bi said to Gao Jiong, "In the past Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou favored music and women and the state perished. Compared with today, is it not even worse?"

At that time the emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns. Bi said to Gao Jiong, "In the past the Tianyuan Emperor of Zhou favored music and women and the state perished. Compared with today, is it not even worse?"
s0205 周天元 is Zhou's Tianyuan Emperor (Xuan), not Emperor Wu (武帝).

At that time the Emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns; Bi said to Gao Jiong: "In the past Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou favored music and women and the state perished—compared with today, is it not even more so?"

At that time the Emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns; Bi said to Gao Jiong: "In the past the Tianyuan Emperor of Zhou favored music and women and the state perished—compared with today, is it not even more so?"
s0205 天元 names the Tianyuan Emperor of Zhou, not Emperor Wu.
He was appointed pillar of state, granted a hundred thirty slaves and maidservants, five hundred bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
He was appointed kaifu, granted a hundred thirty slaves and maidservants, five hundred bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
s0227 拜開府 is appointment to kaifu, not 柱國 pillar of state.
He was appointed Pillar of State, granted 130 slaves and maidservants, 500 bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
He was appointed Kaifu, granted 130 slaves and maidservants, 500 bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
s0227 開府 is kaifu rank, not Pillar of State.
Minister of rites Yang Xuangan's envoy arrived at Jiangdu. That man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan arrived on a mission at Jiangdu. That man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.

Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan's envoy arrived at Jiangdu; that man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan arrived on a mission at Jiangdu; that man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.

His father Chen held the rank Equal to the Three Excellencies. When Wang became honored, Chen was posthumously granted duke of Pingxiang county.
